newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees oil refining capacity doubled in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: India sees oil refining capacity doubled in 5 yrs.

text.p: India is expected to double its crude oil refining capacity in the next five years with an investment of some 700 billion rupees, junior petroleum minister T.R. Balu said on Tuesday.
He told an energy conference in New Delhi that India was expected to attain a refining capacity of 131 million tonnes a year by 2001/02 (April-March) from the current 61.55 million.

Balu said state-owned firms, acting alone as well as with private partners, were expected to add 45 million tonnes of annual capacity by 2001/02. Private companies on their own were expected to add some 24 million tonnes of capacity, he said.
Balu said by the year 2006/07, annual refining capacity was expected to rise to 173 million tonnes.
He also said domestic natural gas production was growing 20 percent a year, and output was now 65 million cubic metres per day.
The share of natural gas in total energy consumption was forecast to rise to 11 percent in 2010 from the current level of eight percent, he added.
"In fact, there is a view that natural gas may become the dominant fuel in the 21st century," Balu said.
Balu said all efforts were being made to import natural gas and liquefied natural gas to supplement limited domestic availability.
He said hydroelectricity and nuclear power were expected to "remain at the present low level of exploitation", while non-conventional sources such as wind, solar power and biomass had good potential.
"With the escalating cost of commercial energy and the environmental costs, non-conventional energy seems to be a viable option as we step towards the 21st century," Balu said.

India needs a coordinated effort from the private and public sectors to meet its demand for petroleum products of about 113 million tonnes by the year 2000, Balu said. He gave no figure for current demand.
"The policy initiatives made by the government are intended to attract as many players as possible into this gigantic effort," Balu said.
